consent.title: One quick question
consent.what: Ember saves your habit names, check-ins, low days, day notes, habit notes, moods, slips with the reasons you give, and your “What helps me” list. They can say something about your health (think “take my meds”, “sleep 8 hours” or a reason like “stressed”). Under the GDPR (Article 9) that counts as health data, so Ember asks before saving it.
consent.why: Ember stores it only to run your habit tracker for you. It's never sold or used for ads. It reaches only the services Ember runs on: Cloudflare passes on the connection to Ember and sees the data unencrypted while doing so, and Discord gets your reminders if you use it for them. The operator has technical access to the server. The operator's usage numbers come only from account and sign-in data such as sign-in times and app version, never from your health data. Fireside asks for its own consent when you turn it on. You can withdraw your consent any time in Settings under “Privacy”: Ember then saves nothing new, reminders stop, and you can only export your data. After 30 days Ember deletes it, with a reminder a few days before. Backups are gone within about 6 weeks.
consent.without: Without it, Ember saves nothing new and sends no reminders. You can still export what you have. If you don't agree within 30 days, Ember deletes it, with a reminder a few days before. Your account and settings stay.

about.intro: Ember is a calm companion for hard moments and gentle days: a short practice when panic, worry or anger gets too big, and gentle habits for the rest.
about.moment.heading: When a moment gets too big
about.moment.text: Tap “I need a moment”. Ember asks what's going on and walks you through a short practice, like slow breathing or 5-4-3-2-1. It works without an account and offline. Nothing from it is saved unless you choose to keep a note in your private journal.
about.habits.heading: On the other days
about.habits.text: Gentle habits: small things like a glass of water or ten pages of reading, with friendly reminders. A rough day doesn't count against you. Mark it as a low day or check in later, and streaks are up to you. There's a journal with moods too, end-to-end encrypted if you like.
about.privacy.heading: Your data
about.privacy.text: With an account, your habits stay in sync on the web, in the Android app and in Discord. Without one, your data stays on this device only.
about.beta: Ember is still in beta and isn't a medical service. In an emergency, call 112.
landing.lede: {{description}} When it gets loud, Ember stays with you for a few steady minutes: name what's happening, breathe, ride it out. No account needed, and nothing from a moment is kept unless you choose to save it.
landing.talk: Need someone to talk to right now?
landing.madeBy: Free. Made by Nico, a developer in Germany.
landing.screenshotAlt: Ember's Today screen: the “I need a moment” door above the habits, three of them checked in today.
landing.feature.reminders.title: Reminders that nudge, not nag
landing.feature.reminders.text: A notification at the times you pick, with a Done button right in it. Yesterday stays open, so a forgotten check-in is easy to fill in.
landing.feature.platforms.title: On the web and on Android
landing.feature.platforms.text: Check in from any browser, or use the Android app with reminders that work offline and a home-screen widget.
landing.feature.flexible.title: Habits that bend
landing.feature.flexible.text: Daily, weekdays, a few times a week or several times a day. Call a hard day a low day. Streaks stay off unless you want them.
landing.feature.private.title: Private by design
landing.feature.private.text: Try it without an account and your data stays on this device. Keep an end-to-end encrypted journal, and export everything any time.
landing.extra.journal.title: A journal and moods
landing.extra.journal.text: Jot a line about your day and pick how it felt. Add your own moods next to the five built-in ones.
landing.extra.themes.title: Four themes, light and dark
landing.extra.themes.text: Hearthlight, Fieldnotes, Tidepool and Marigold, each in light and dark. Pick the one that feels like yours.
landing.extra.discord.title: Use Discord? Bring Ember along
landing.extra.discord.text: If you like, add the Ember bot for reminders in your DMs and quick check-ins there. You can sign in with Discord too.

guide.title: {{screen}}, explained
guide.habit.name: Habits
guide.today.lede: Your habits for today, and a quiet moment when things get too much.
guide.today.checkIn.q: What do “1/2” and the empty circle mean?
guide.today.checkIn.a: An empty circle is a habit you do once a day and haven't checked in yet. Tap it to check in. A habit you do more than once a day shows your count, like 1/2, and each tap adds one until it's done.
guide.today.weekly.q: What does “2 of 3 this week” mean?
guide.today.weekly.a: That's a habit you do a few times a week. Every day you check in counts once, from Monday to Sunday, until you reach your target. Which days is up to you. Once you've reached it on an earlier day, it waits under Not for today with Done for this week.
guide.today.lowDay.a: A low day is for days that are hard. It covers all the habits you're building up: streaks neither break nor grow, the day counts as kept, and that day's reminders stay quiet. You can also mark an earlier day in History, just not a future one.
guide.today.reminders.q: When will Ember remind me, and can I check in ahead?
guide.today.reminders.a: At the reminder times you set for each habit, on the days it's planned; a habit in a routine with its own reminder time is reminded by the routine instead. Once you've checked in enough for the day, or for the week with weekly habits, the rest stay quiet. So feel free to check in early; only future days can't be filled in. A habit you're letting go of only gets its one quiet check-in, if you pick a time. If you withdraw your consent or choose No thanks, reminders stop.
guide.today.moment.a: A few quiet minutes for when panic, worry or anger gets too big. Ember walks you through a short practice, like slow breathing, with or without an account. Nothing from it is saved unless you keep a reflection in your private journal.
guide.history.lede: Look back at one habit month by month, and fill in days you missed.
guide.history.fillIn.q: Can I fill in a day I missed?
guide.history.fillIn.a: Yes. Tap any day from the habit's start up to today to mark it done or not done, or to clear it. Filling in an older day updates your streak too. For a habit you're letting go of, tap a day to note a slip there or remove it, or to mark a day without as made it.
guide.history.lowDay.q: Can I mark a low day afterwards?
guide.history.lowDay.a: Yes. Tap the day, then Mark as a low day. It applies to all the habits you're building up and works for today and earlier days, not future ones.
guide.history.kept.a: It counts the days you kept this habit lately: the days you checked in, plus low days on its planned days. A day that's only partly done doesn't count yet.
guide.history.streaks.a: With streaks on, a streak counts the days in a row you kept a daily or set-day habit. Low days, pauses and rest days never break it, and today and yesterday stay open, so they don't count as missed yet. Grace days can cover a few other gaps. Habits you're letting go of count days without instead.
guide.history.year.q: What does the year view show?
guide.history.year.a: Your past year as one heatmap, for all the habits you're building up, or just one. Switch to it with Year.
guide.habit.lede: How often a habit comes up, how it reminds you, and how to take a break.
guide.habit.frequency.q: “On set days” or “A few times a week”?
guide.habit.frequency.a: On set days means fixed weekdays you pick, like Monday and Thursday. The other days are rest days. A few times a week means a weekly target instead: any day you check in counts once, from Monday to Sunday.
guide.habit.timesADay.a: It's for habits you do more than once a day, like drinking water, up to {{max}} times. Each tap on Today adds one and shows your count, like 1/2. You can set a reminder time for each check-in.
guide.habit.limits.q: How many habits can I have, and how long can names be?
guide.habit.limits.a: You can have up to {{habits}} habits. A name can be up to {{name}} characters, and a counter shows up as you get close.
guide.habit.pause.q: Can I take a break from a habit?
guide.habit.pause.a: Yes. On a habit's edit page, Take a break pauses it until a day you choose. Reminders stop meanwhile, and your streak or your days without are kept.
guide.routines.lede: Habits you do together, under one name and one reminder.
guide.routines.what.a: A group of habits you do together, like a morning routine, in the order you do them. Today shows them together under the routine's name, as one block you can move.
guide.routines.reminder.q: How does a routine's reminder work?
guide.routines.reminder.a: A routine can have one reminder time. It nudges you once for the habits in it that are still open that day (plus the second reminder, if you use it), and it replaces their own reminders while they're in the routine.
guide.routines.one.q: Can a habit be in more than one routine?
guide.routines.one.a: No, a habit is in one routine at a time. Adding it to another routine moves it there.
guide.routines.limits.q: How many routines can I have?
guide.routines.limits.a: Up to {{routines}} routines, with names of up to {{name}} characters. Deleting a routine keeps its habits and their check-ins.
guide.routines.order.q: How do I change the order on Today?
guide.routines.order.a: At first Today sorts by reminder time, earliest first, and a routine uses its own time; anything without a time comes after, by name. Hold a row for a moment and drag it, or use Move up and Move down in its menu. A routine moves as one block. Ember remembers your order. Inside a routine, this changes the routine's own order. Sort by time again, in the list's menu, goes back.
guide.settings.lede: Everything you can change, sorted into a few groups.
guide.settings.streaks.q: Where do I turn streaks on or off?
guide.settings.streaks.a: In Habits & days, with Show streaks. Grace days are in the same group while streaks are on.
guide.settings.looks.q: Where do I change how Ember looks?
guide.settings.looks.a: In Appearance: language, light or dark, your theme and calm mode. In the Android app, Gentle motion for the widget is there too.
guide.settings.helpRightNow.q: Is “Help right now” the same as this guide?
guide.settings.helpRightNow.a: No. Help right now is for hard moments: crisis lines for your region, any time of day. This guide only explains how Ember works.
guide.settings.sync.q: Do my habits sync between devices?
guide.settings.sync.a: With an account, yes: the web app, the Android app and Discord share your habits and check-ins. Without an account, everything stays on this device, and you can export a backup any time.
guide.settings.down.a: Sometimes Ember's server takes a short break. A short notice may show at the top then. The app keeps what's already on your device, and check-ins you make in the meantime are saved on your device and sync once Ember is back. “I need a moment” and Urgent help keep working the whole time.
guide.reminders.lede: Where Ember can reach you, and when it stays quiet.
guide.reminders.when.a: At the reminder times on each habit or routine, on the days they're planned. Once you've checked in enough for the day, or for the week with weekly habits, Ember stays quiet. A low day or a pause quiets them too. A habit you're letting go of gets just one quiet check-in, if you pick a time, and only a pause quiets it.
guide.reminders.where.a: With an account: in a browser, in the Android app and by Discord DM, if you use Discord. Each habit and routine uses every place that's on, unless you untick one when you edit it. Without an account, the Android app reminds you on that phone.
guide.reminders.tap.q: What happens when I tap a reminder?
guide.reminders.tap.a: It opens Today, and on your phone it goes straight to that habit. A reminder for a single habit also has a Done button that adds a check-in for you. The quiet check-in for a habit you're letting go of opens that habit and has no buttons.
guide.reminders.second.a: If you still haven't checked in, Ember nudges you once more after the wait you pick here. It comes only once, and only on the same day. Habits you're letting go of never get one.
guide.habitsDays.lede: Streaks, grace days and the timezone your days follow.
guide.habitsDays.streaks.a: It counts the days in a row you kept each daily or set-day habit, on Today and in History. Habits you do a few times a week show their weekly count instead. Turned off, Ember shows your check-ins without counting. Habits you're letting go of always show their days without.
guide.habitsDays.grace.a: With streaks on, a few days without a check-in don't break a daily or set-day habit's streak. You pick how many in any seven days, up to {{max}}. They happen on their own, so there's nothing to mark.
guide.habitsDays.kinds.q: Grace day, low day or pause: what's the difference?
guide.habitsDays.kinds.a: Grace days happen on their own. A low day is one you mark yourself, and it covers all the habits you're building up. A pause is for one habit, until a day you choose.
guide.habitsDays.timezone.a: Your days follow it: “today” starts at midnight there, and reminders go out at its local time. Change it if you move.
guide.appearance.lede: How Ember looks and moves on your screen.
guide.appearance.themes.a: Each theme has its own colors and fonts, in a light and a dark version. With an account, your theme follows you to your other devices.
guide.appearance.lightDark.q: Why is light or dark different on my other device?
guide.appearance.lightDark.a: Light or dark is set on each device, so every device can have its own. System follows the device's own setting.
guide.appearance.calm.a: Calm mode turns off motion, softens the colors and hides extra decorations. Breathing in “I need a moment” shows text only.
guide.privacy.lede: What stays private, and how to take your data with you or delete it.
guide.privacy.journal.a: With an account, your journal is private to your account, but Ember's server stores it as plain text. Turn on the private journal and your entries, habit notes and own moods are encrypted on your device before they're sent, so only you can read them, not even Ember's server. Without an account, it stays on this device.
guide.privacy.passphrase.q: What if I forget my passphrase?
guide.privacy.passphrase.a: With an account and the private journal on, your recovery code opens the journal too. You see that code only once, when you turn the journal on. If you lose both, nobody can open it again, Ember included.
guide.privacy.helps.a: With an account and the private journal on, you can keep a short list of what helped you before. While the journal is unlocked on this device, the first few show up when you open “I need a moment”. Only you can read the list.
guide.privacy.export.q: Can I take my data with me?
guide.privacy.export.a: Yes. With an account, download your data as JSON or CSV under Your data, on the web. Anything in your private journal stays encrypted in that file, and the journal has its own decrypted export. Without an account, export a backup under On this device.
guide.privacy.delete.a: Deleting your account removes it and everything in it, and it can't be undone. Without an account, you delete everything on this device instead. Save a copy first if you'd like to keep one. To keep your account, withdraw your consent under Privacy instead: Ember then keeps your habits and entries for export only and deletes them later, after a reminder.

letgo.form.checkInHint: Off unless you pick a time. Then Ember checks in once that evening, quietly, and never a second time.

letgo.sheet.title: Noting a slip
letgo.sheet.body: It happens, and it doesn't undo the days behind you. Want to note what was going on?
letgo.sheet.journal: Add a note to today's journal
letgo.tryInstead.heading: Try instead
letgo.tryInstead.stepOutside: Step outside for a few minutes
letgo.tryInstead.phoneAway: Put the phone in another room
letgo.noted_one: Noted. Your longest stretch so far is {{count}} day.
letgo.noted_other: Noted. Your longest stretch so far is {{count}} days.
letgo.notedFirst: Noted. Every day is a new start.
letgo.undone: Taken back. Today has no slips noted.
letgo.undoFailed: That couldn't be undone just now
letgo.day.add: Note a slip on this day
letgo.day.mark: Mark this day as made it
letgo.reminder.body: A quiet check-in for {{name}}. If anything happened today, you can note it in Ember.
letgo.reminder.bodyNameless: A quiet check-in. If anything happened today, you can note it in Ember.
guide.habit.letGo.q: What is a habit to let go of?
guide.habit.letGo.a: Something you want to stop or do less. Instead of a streak it counts days without, and it has its own section on Today, called Letting go, below For today. On a day without, you can tap “Made it today” if it feels good; it's just for you and changes no count. It has no schedule and can't be in a routine. If you like, Ember checks in quietly once a day at a time you pick. Below the section, “Try instead” offers a few gentle ideas for the moment.
guide.habitsDays.slip.a: Tap “I slipped” and Save; a reason is optional. A slip is never a failure: your longest stretch and this month's days without stay, and days without start again from the next day. After saving, Ember shows a few things to try instead: your own “What helps me” list while your private journal is unlocked, otherwise a short list of its own. In the Android app it can also open your phone's own screen-time overview; Ember reads nothing from it. Paused days count as neither a day without nor a slip. Noted it by mistake? Undo takes it back, and in History you can remove a day's slips. Noting a slip on a day marked “Made it today” takes that mark away.
fireside.title: Fireside
fireside.loadFailed: Your fireside couldn't load just now.
fireside.settings.intro: Add a few people you trust and send each other a little warmth now and then.
fireside.settings.privacy: They see your name, when you ask for warmth, and, if you allow it for them, whether you checked in today. Your habits, moods, journal and moments stay yours. Nobody is told when you read something, and nothing needs an answer.
fireside.consent.title: Before you turn on Fireside
fireside.consent.body: At Fireside you share things with the people you link: your name, “Could use some warmth today” when you ask for it, and, if you allow it per person, whether you checked in today. Asking for warmth and your check-in status can say something about how you're doing and so count as health data (GDPR Art. 9). With “Agree and turn on” you explicitly agree that Ember shares them with your links. You can withdraw this any time by turning Fireside off or by taking back a person's flame.
fireside.settings.name: Your name at the fireside
fireside.settings.nameHint: Your friends see this. Up to {{max}} characters.
fireside.settings.nameInvalid: Use 1 to {{max}} characters, without invisible characters.
fireside.settings.offConfirm: You leave every fireside, and your Fireside consent ends.

fireside.friends.helper: You can send each friend warmth once a day, and once more when they ask for some. Tap a name to mute or remove them.

fireside.joinedNotice.explain: “Not someone I know” removes them right away and turns your code off. They aren't told why.
fireside.joinedNotice.removed: {{name}} is no longer at your fireside, and your code is off.
fireside.add.title: Add a friend
fireside.add.lede: One of you shows a code, the other types it in. That's it, no requests.
fireside.add.quiet: Nobody can find you any other way. A new code turns the old one off.
fireside.code.none: No code to show right now.

fireside.join.invalid: That code didn't work. Ask for a new one.
fireside.join.joinedText: You can send each other warmth now. {{name}} sees your name, nothing else.
fireside.notify.label: Notify me about warmth and new friends
fireside.notify.hint: Off by default. When it's on, warmth and new friends reach you where your reminders do, in this browser or on Discord.
fireside.notify.android: In the Android app, warmth shows here and on Today when you open Ember. There are no notifications on Android yet.

fireside.friend.removeHint: You disappear from each other's fireside. {{name}} isn't told. To find each other again, one of you would need a new code.

fireside.send.pick: Pick one. {{name}} sees it with your name.
fireside.warmth.quiet: {{name}} isn't told when you read this.

fireside.ask.names_one: {{names}} will see “Could use some warmth today” next to your name until midnight. They won't see why, or anything about this moment.
fireside.ask.names_other: {{names}} will see “Could use some warmth today” next to your name until midnight. They won't see why, or anything about this moment.

fireside.ask.failed: That didn't go through just now. You can turn it on later on Today.
fireside.ask.todayHint: Your friends see this next to your name until midnight, never why.

fireside.merge.dropped_other: {{count}} Fireside friends won't come along (you already share them, or you'd go over {{max}}). Your own friends all stay.
guide.fireside.lede: A few people you trust, a little warmth, no pressure.
guide.fireside.what.a: A quiet place for a few people you trust, up to {{friends}}. You send each other warmth, one of a few short messages, and can say when you could use some. Nobody sees whether you read it, and nothing needs an answer. Turn it on in Settings, under People; Ember asks for your consent first. It needs an Ember account.
guide.fireside.sees.a: Your Fireside name, always. “Could use some warmth today” on days you ask for it, until midnight, never why. A small flame on days you check in, only for friends you turn it on for, and never which habits. Your habits, moods, journal and moments stay yours. If you mute or remove someone, they aren't told.
guide.fireside.codes.a: One of you makes a code, the other types it in. A code has {{length}} letters and numbers, works once and only for {{minutes}} minutes, and a new code turns the old one off. If someone joins you don't know, choose Not someone I know: they're removed and your code stops working.
